rows.description: An old friend reaches out after years and I feel pleased, wary, and a little resentful of the gap. I meet them with warmth and honesty, let trust return slowly, and neither pretend no time passed nor punish them.

rows.description: My best friend shared my secret with others and I feel humiliated and enraged. I tell them clearly what happened and how it hurt, watch how they respond, and decide the friendship's future by their repair and not by my anger.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, forgiveness, guilt, loyalty, manipulation, trust
related mind states: anger, humiliation, hurt

rows.description: I repeated a friend's secret to others and now feel sick with guilt. The honest path is to tell them before they hear it elsewhere, apologise without excuses, and accept whatever distance they need.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, exploitation, forgiveness, loyalty, manipulation, trust

rows.description: I share someone's private trouble over chai because it feels like bonding. I ask whether they would want it told, and choose to earn closeness through my own honesty and not through the currency of others' secrets.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, exploitation, forgiveness, guilt, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: A friend has trusted me with something risky or painful. I feel the weight of it, keep it safe, and if their safety is truly at stake I urge them toward help before considering telling anyone else.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, exploitation, forgiveness, guilt, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: My friend does something wrong or is cheating on a partner and confides in me. I feel torn. I tell them honestly what I think and refuse to lie for them, without publicly exposing them or cutting them off.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, exploitation, forgiveness, guilt, manipulation, trust

rows.description: A friend only calls when they need money, favours, or a place to stay, and I feel used. I can give within limits, say no without long explanations, and notice that a friendship without mutual care is thin.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, forgiveness, guilt, loyalty, manipulation, trust

rows.description: A friend apologised for a serious breach and I am not sure I can trust again. I can forgive without full reconciliation; I decide the level of closeness based on actions over time, not on words or guilt.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, exploitation, guilt, loyalty, manipulation, trust

rows.description: A friend uses emotional pressure, sulking, or guilt to get their way and I feel confused about my own feelings. I name the pattern calmly, hold my boundary, and pull back if they punish me for having a limit.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, exploitation, forgiveness, guilt, loyalty, trust

rows.description: My co-founder was my close friend and I now doubt everything we built. I separate the sting of the betrayal from the value of the work, gather facts, and document agreements; sadness is fair, panic decisions are not.
